mainTopic: Limits on blocking outside sellers, the story of רב אדא בר אבא's death, and the new משנה about distancing walls four אמות
overview: The amud opens by finishing the earlier rule about teachers: rivalry among teachers increases wisdom, so one teacher cannot block another. The גמרא then limits רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's rule that townspeople may block outside businesses. Traveling peddlers cannot be blocked, because of a תקנה of עזרא, but they may not open a fixed shop unless they are תלמידי חכמים. Next come cases about outside sellers. רבינא lets basket sellers sell to visitors on market day, in the market only. רב כהנא lets wool sellers sell only enough to live on until they collect their debts. A long story follows: רב אדא בר אבא tests רב דימי with a hard question, and as a result the market is not held for רב דימי and his figs spoil. When רב אדא בר אבא later dies, five חכמים each say it happened because of them, and the גמרא concludes it was רב נחמן בר יצחק. Finally, a new משנה requires keeping a wall four אמות from a neighbor's wall and windows. The גמרא asks how the first wall was built close, and רב יהודה's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Competition among teachers increases wisdom
steps.stepSummary: The closing reason of the earlier opinion that one teacher cannot block another teacher from opening nearby: rivalry among teachers increases wisdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Jealousy among teachers increases wisdom.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the discussion from the previous page about teachers of young children. It gives the reason why one teacher cannot stop a new teacher from opening nearby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ordinary business, a new competitor can hurt an existing seller. With Torah teaching, competition pushes every teacher to do a better job, so the children gain. That is why the usual right to block a competitor does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: Jealousy or rivalry among teachers and scholars

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a famous principle: in Torah learning, healthy competition is welcomed rather than blocked.

phrases.english: Jealousy among teachers increases wisdom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion about teachers, which began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Teachers may not block competing teachers, because competition improves Torah learning.

steps.title: Even רב הונא agrees traveling peddlers cannot be blocked
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, who lets townspeople block outsiders, agrees that traveling peddlers cannot be blocked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Even רב הונא son of רב יהושע agrees about peddlers who travel from town to town that the townspeople cannot stop them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, who said townspeople may keep an outsider from doing business in their town. רב נחמן בר יצחק points out one case where even רב הונא agrees they cannot: traveling peddlers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule from רב הונא favors the local residents. This step adds an exception. Traveling peddlers (רוכלין) may come in, and the town cannot stop them.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees (even someone with a stricter view concedes this point)
Peddlers who sell perfumes, jewelry and cosmetics
Who travel around from town to town
Is able to prevent or block

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹדֶה רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: And Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, concedes
phrases.notes: רב הונא is the one who said earlier that people from a town can stop an outsider from doing business there.

phrases.english: regarding peddlers who travel around the towns,
that one cannot prevent them;

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב הונא's rule about blocking outsiders and adds an exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Traveling peddlers cannot be blocked from entering a town, even according to רב הונא.

steps.title: The source: עזרא's enactment for peddlers
steps.stepSummary: The reason is a תקנה of עזרא: peddlers should travel from town to town so that jewelry and cosmetics are available to Jewish women.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: עזרא enacted for the Jewish people that peddlers should travel around the towns, so that jewelry would be available to Jewish women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the exception with a source: a תקנה of עזרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עזרא wanted Jewish women everywhere to have access to jewelry and cosmetics. A town cannot block what עזרא specifically set up, so the peddlers keep their right to travel and sell.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a rabbinic enactment can override the ordinary rights of local businesses.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
Ezra enacted for the Jewish people
that peddlers should travel around the towns,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהוּ תַּכְשִׁיטִין מְצוּיִין לִבְנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: so that jewelry would be available to Jewish women.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר: עֶזְרָא תִּקֵּן לָהֶן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the exception in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that traveling peddlers cannot be blocked.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עזרא's enactment that peddlers travel from town to town for the sake of Jewish women.

steps.title: Only for traveling, not for opening a fixed shop
steps.stepSummary: The peddlers' protection covers only traveling around. A peddler who wants to open a permanent shop in town can be blocked.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only to traveling around. But to set up a fixed shop, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the peddlers' right. It covers traveling from place to place, but not settling down with a permanent store.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עזרא's goal was met by peddlers who pass through. A permanent shop goes beyond what the תקנה needed, so רב הונא's normal rule applies again and the town may block it.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply only to (a limiting phrase)
To set oneself up permanently (open a fixed shop)

phrases.english: And this applies only to traveling around,
but to set up a fixed shop, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the exception from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A peddler may travel around a town but may be blocked from opening a permanent shop.

steps.title: A תלמיד חכם may even open a fixed shop
steps.stepSummary: If the peddler is a Torah scholar (צורבא מרבנן), he may even set up a permanent shop.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he is a Torah scholar, he may even set up a fixed shop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds an exception to the limit in step 4. A Torah scholar may open a permanent shop as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said a peddler cannot settle down with a fixed shop. This step makes a special allowance for a צורבא מרבנן. The reason comes in step 8.

phrases.english: And if he is a Torah scholar,
even setting up a fixed shop is also allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes an exception to the limit in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Torah scholar peddler may open a permanent shop in a town.

steps.title: רבא's precedent with two rabbis
steps.stepSummary: רבא allowed רבי יאשיה and רב עובדיה to open fixed shops, even though the strict law would not allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case in which רבא permitted רבי יאשיה and רב עובדיה to set up fixed shops, which was not according to the strict law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the scholar exception with a real story about רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא let two rabbis set up shop in a place where an ordinary person could be blocked. "Not according to the strict law" tells us that this was a special privilege for scholars, beyond the regular rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Not according to the regular law (a special allowance)

steps.confusionAlert: "דלא כהלכתא" does not mean רבא made a mistake. It means he gave the scholars a privilege beyond the ordinary rule.

phrases.english: Like that case in which Rava permitted
Rabbi Yoshiya and Rav Ovadya to set up fixed shops,
not according to the regular law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 5 with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a Torah scholar may open a fixed shop.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's permission to רבי יאשיה and רב עובדיה.

steps.title: Why do scholars get this privilege?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the special allowance for scholars.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why scholars are allowed something that others are not. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a clarifying question, not an attack. The גמרא wants to know what makes a scholar's case different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind steps 5 and 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a Torah scholar may open a fixed shop when others may not.

steps.title: So they are not pulled away from their learning
steps.stepSummary: Since they are scholars, traveling around would pull them away from their Torah study.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they are rabbis, they would be distracted from their learning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that making scholars travel from town to town would take them away from their studies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary peddler can travel. For a scholar, traveling means losing learning time, so he is allowed a fixed shop where he can sell and still keep learning.
steps.whatToRemember: Peddlers may travel through any town because of עזרא's תקנה, but only a תלמיד חכם may open a fixed shop, so that his learning is not disturbed.

phrases.english: Since they are rabbis,
they would come to be distracted from their learning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Scholars would lose learning time if they had to travel, so they may open fixed shops.

steps.title: Basket sellers blocked in בבל
steps.stepSummary: Basket sellers brought baskets to בבל. The locals tried to block them, and both sides came to רבינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were basket sellers who brought baskets to בבל. The townspeople came and tried to block them. They came before רבינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about outside sellers. This step sets up the case that רבינא will rule on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another case of locals blocking outsiders, which connects to רב הונא's rule. The question presented to רבינא is whether the locals may stop them.

phrases.english: There were these basket sellers who brought baskets to Babylonia.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתוֹ בְּנֵי מָתָא קָא מְעַכְּבִי עִלָּוַיְהוּ.
phrases.english: The townspeople came and were blocking them.
They came before Ravina,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case about outside sellers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the townspeople may block the outside basket sellers.

steps.title: רבינא: outsiders may sell to outsiders
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rules that the basket sellers came from outside and may sell to outside buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: They came from outside, so let them sell to outsiders.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives his ruling: outside sellers may sell to customers who are themselves from outside the town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling to visitors does not take customers away from the local sellers in the same way. So the locals have no right to block it.

phrases.english: He said to them:
They came from outside, and let them sell to outsiders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבינא's ruling on the case in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Outside sellers may sell to outside buyers.

steps.title: Only on market day
steps.stepSummary: רבינא's permission applies only on market day, not on other days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only on market day, but not on a day that is not market day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רבינא's ruling to market day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On market day, visitors from other towns come to buy, so the outside sellers have outside customers. On other days the buyers would mostly be locals, so the sellers may be blocked.

phrases.english: And this applies only on market day,
but not on a day that is not market day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבינא's ruling from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Outside sellers may sell only on market day.

steps.title: Even on market day, only in the market
steps.stepSummary: Even on market day, outside sellers may sell only in the marketplace, not by going around the town.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even on market day, we only said this for selling in the market, but not for going around the town.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more limit. Even on market day, the outsiders must stay in the market and may not go door to door.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The market is where the visiting buyers are. Going around the town would reach local customers and take business from local sellers, so it stays forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: Outside sellers may sell to visitors on market day, but only in the market itself. They may not sell on other days or go around the town selling.

phrases.english: And even on market day we did not say this
except for selling in the market,
but for going around, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the market-day permission from step 11 even further.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Outside sellers may sell only on market day and only in the marketplace, not by going around the town.

steps.title: Wool sellers are blocked in פום נהרא
steps.stepSummary: Outside wool sellers bring wool to פום נהרא, the locals block them, and both sides come to רב כהנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some wool sellers brought wool to פום נהרא. The townspeople tried to stop them from selling, and they came to רב כהנא to decide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case about outside sellers and sets it up for a ruling by רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works like the basket sellers in step 9: outsiders come in, locals object, and a רב is asked to rule. The case is now in front of רב כהנא, and his answer comes next.

phrases.english: There were these wool sellers
who brought wool to Pum Nahara.
The townspeople came
and were blocking them.
They came before Rav Kahana.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ עָמוֹרָאֵי דְּאַיְיתוֹ עַמְרָא לְפוּם נַהֲרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case about outside sellers, parallel to the basket sellers in steps 9-12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May the townspeople stop outside wool sellers from selling in their town?

steps.title: רב כהנא sides with the townspeople
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rules that the locals are allowed to block the outside sellers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The law is that they may stop you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives his ruling: the townspeople are right to block the wool sellers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the basic rule from earlier steps: locals may protect their market from outsiders. רב כהנא applies that plain rule here, and the sellers' answer in the next step is what changes the outcome.

phrases.english: He said to them:
The law is that they may block you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the case raised in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the townspeople may block outside sellers.

steps.title: The sellers say they have debts to collect
steps.stepSummary: The wool sellers push back: people in town owe them money, so they need to stay.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We have debts owed to us here!
steps.whatsHappening: The wool sellers argue against the ruling. They have a special reason to be in town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They are not just outsiders looking for business. They must stay to collect money owed to them, and they need to live while they wait. This challenges a full ban on their selling.

phrases.english: They said to him:
We have debts owed to us here!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against רב כהנא's ruling in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's ruling that the sellers may be fully blocked.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: They must stay to collect their debts, so a total ban leaves them unable to support themselves.

steps.title: Sell only enough to live on until the debts are paid
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא lets them sell just enough to support themselves until they collect their debts, and then they must leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Go sell enough to live on until you collect your debts, and then leave.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא accepts their point in a limited way. They may sell a little, but only while they collect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule still stands: locals may block outsiders. The exception is narrow. They may sell only what they need to live, and only until their debts are collected.

keyTerms.meaning: The amount you need to live on

steps.whatToRemember: Outside sellers may be blocked, but if they must stay in town to collect debts, they may sell enough to live on until they leave.

phrases.english: He said to them: Go sell
the amount you need to live on
until you collect your debts,
and then leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the sellers' objection from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limited exception within the general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A total ban, so the sellers cannot sell anything at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: They may sell enough to live on, and only until their debts are collected.

steps.title: Should the market be held for רב דימי?
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי brings figs by ship. ריש גלותא tells רבא to reserve the market for him if he is a scholar, and רבא sends רב אדא בר אבא to test him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי from נהרדעא brought dried figs on a ship. ריש גלותא told רבא: Go check, and if he is a תלמיד חכם, hold the market for him. רבא told רב אדא בר אבא: Go test him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story that sets up a test of whether רב דימי is a scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scholars get a market privilege: other sellers wait so the scholar can sell first. To give that privilege, someone must first check that the person really is a scholar. That check comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, leader of the Jews in בבל

phrases.english: Rav Dimi from Nehardea
brought dried figs on a ship.
The Exilarch said to Rava:
Go and see,
if he is a Torah scholar,
hold the market for him.
phrases.notes: Meaning: keep other fig sellers out so he can sell his figs first.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Adda bar Abba:
Go smell his jar.
phrases.notes: An expression: test him to see what's inside, like smelling a jug to check the wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story, connected to the scholar's privilege mentioned around step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם may have the market held for him, but first he must be confirmed as a scholar.

steps.title: The test question about the elephant and the basket
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אבא asks רב דימי a hard question about a basket that passed through an elephant, and רב דימי cannot answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and asked him: An elephant swallowed an Egyptian wicker basket and passed it out with its waste. What is the law? רב דימי did not know.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the test. רב אדא בר אבא asks a hard halachic question, and רב דימי has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether a basket that went through an animal's digestion is still the same vessel. Not knowing the answer will decide whether רב דימי gets the scholar's privilege.

keyTerms.meaning: The rear opening where waste comes out
He did not have the answer

phrases.english: He went out and asked him:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets, אֲזַל, which also means 'went'.

phrases.english: An elephant that swallowed an Egyptian wicker basket
and passed it out with its waste,
what is the law?
He did not have the answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the test that רבא ordered in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a basket that passed through an elephant stay the same vessel for טומאה?

steps.title: "Are you רבא?" and רב אדא בר אבא's sharp reply
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי asks if he is speaking to רבא. רב אדא בר אבא taps his sandal and says that even he, רבא's student, is רב דימי's teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Are you רבא? רב אדא tapped him on his sandal and said: There is a big gap between me and רבא, but either way I am your teacher, and רבא is your teacher's teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי is amazed by the hard question. רב אדא בר אבא answers in a way that puts him down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי hints that only someone as great as רבא could ask such a question. רב אדא replies that since he just stumped רב דימי, he counts as his teacher, which makes רבא his teacher's teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: He tapped him on his sandal, a gesture of putting him down
Like it or not, either way

phrases.english: He said to him: Is the master Rava?
phrases.notes: He means: are you רבא, since only someone that great could ask this?

phrases.english: He tapped him on his sandal,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בֵּין דִּידִי לְרָבָא אִיכָּא טוּבָא,
phrases.english: and said to him: Between me and Rava there is a great deal of difference,
but either way, I am your teacher,
and Rava is your teacher's teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The exchange that follows רב דימי's failure to answer in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since רב דימי could not answer, רב אדא בר אבא judged that he was not a great scholar.

steps.title: The figs spoil and רב דימי complains to רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The market is not held for רב דימי, his figs are lost, and he complains to רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: They did not hold the market for him, and his dried figs were lost. He came to רב יוסף and said: Look what they did to me!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the result of the test and sets up רב יוסף's response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he did not pass the test, he lost the scholar's privilege and his figs spoiled. Now he brings his complaint to רב יוסף.

phrases.english: They did not hold the market for him,
and his dried figs were lost.
He came before Rav Yosef

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזִי מָר מַאי עֲבַדוּ לִי!
phrases.english: and said to him: Let the master see what they did to me!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The outcome of the failed test in steps 18-19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without the scholar's privilege, רב דימי's figs spoiled.

steps.title: רב יוסף: ה׳ will not delay answering your shame
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף tells רב דימי that just as ה׳ quickly punished the shaming of the king of אדום, He will quickly answer רב דימי's shame. He brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: The One Who did not delay punishing the shame done to the king of אדום will not delay answering your shame, as it says: "So says ה׳: For three sins of מואב, and for four, I will not take it back, because he burned the bones of the king of אדום into lime."
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף sides with רב דימי and says ה׳ will answer his humiliation, proving it from a פסוק in עמוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ה׳ punished מואב for disgracing even a non-Jewish king's bones, then shaming a תלמיד חכם will surely be answered. This hints that רב דימי was wrongly treated and should have been honored.
steps.whatToRemember: Shaming a תלמיד חכם is serious. ה׳ answers humiliation quickly, as He did for the king of אדום.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The One Who did not delay
answering the shame of the king of Edom
will not delay answering your shame.
phrases.notes: He means ה׳ will soon repay whoever humiliated you.

phrases.english: As it is written: "So says the Lord:
For three sins of Moab
and for four, I will not take it back,

phrases.aramaic: עַל שׇׂרְפוֹ עַצְמוֹת מֶלֶךְ אֱדוֹם לַסִּיד״.
phrases.english: because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב דימי's complaint from step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ will quickly answer the humiliation done to רב דימי, just as He answered the disgrace of the king of אדום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עמוס 2:1, where מואב is punished for burning the bones of the king of אדום.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אבא dies, and רב יוסף takes responsibility
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב אדא בר אבא died. רב יוסף says it came about because of him, since he cursed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אבא died. רב יוסף said: I punished him, because I cursed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that רב אדא בר אבא died. This opens a list of חכמים who each say his death was because of them, starting with רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step, רב יוסף told רב דימי that ה׳ would quickly answer his shame. Now רב יוסף says his own words worked like a curse against רב אדא בר אבא. This begins a series of opinions about what caused the death.

keyTerms.meaning: I punished him, meaning he was punished because of me

steps.confusionAlert: 'אנא ענישתיה' does not mean the speaker planned to hurt him. It means: 'His punishment came about because of something connected to me.'

phrases.aramaic: נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַבָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Abba died.
Rav Yosef said: I punished him,
because I cursed him.
phrases.notes: This points back to רב יוסף's words to רב דימי in the last step, that ה׳ would quickly answer his shame.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַבָּא. רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: אֲנָא עֲנֵישְׁתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the outcome of רב יוסף's statement in step 21: רב אדא בר אבא dies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף says רב אדא בר אבא died because of his curse.

steps.title: רב דימי says the death came because of his lost figs
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי מנהרדעא says he is the cause, because רב אדא בר אבא made him lose his dried figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי from נהרדעא said: I punished him, because he caused me to lose my dried figs.
steps.whatsHappening: A second חכם gives his own reason for the death. רב דימי points to the loss of his figs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף pointed to his curse. רב דימי points to the harm itself: רב אדא בר אבא embarrassed him, so the market was not held for him and his figs were lost (steps 18 to 20).

keyTerms.meaning: נהרדעא, a major Jewish town in Babylonia

phrases.english: Rav Dimi from Nehardea said:
I punished him,
because he caused the loss of my dried figs.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב דִּימִי מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא אָמַר: אֲנָא עֲנֵישְׁתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second claim of responsibility next to רב יוסף's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב דימי says the death came because of the loss of his figs.

steps.title: אביי says the death came because רב אדא belittled his ישיבה
steps.stepSummary: אביי says he is the cause, because רב אדא בר אבא told students that learning with אביי was like gnawing bones, while learning with רבא was like eating fatty meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I punished him, because he told the students: Instead of gnawing bones in אביי's school, come eat fatty meat in רבא's school.
steps.whatsHappening: A third חכם, אביי, says the death was because of him. רב אדא בר אבא had spoken badly of אביי's learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This claim is about honor, not money. רב אדא בר אבא compared אביי's teaching to dry bones and רבא's teaching to rich meat. That disrespect toward a great teacher is given as the cause.

phrases.english: Abaye said: I punished him,
because he said to the Sages:
Instead of gnawing bones in the school of Abaye,
come eat fatty meat in the school of Rava.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'fatty,' is part of the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third claim of responsibility, this time based on disrespect toward a teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי says the death came because רב אדא בר אבא belittled his teaching.

steps.title: רבא says the death came because רב אדא claimed to outrank his servant
steps.stepSummary: רבא says he is the cause, because רב אדא בר אבא would push ahead of רבא's servant at the butcher and say he was greater than him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I punished him. When he went to the butcher to get a piece of meat, he told the butchers: I will take meat before רבא's servant, because I am greater than he is.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth חכם, רבא, says the death was because of him. רב אדא בר אבא would cut in front of רבא's servant at the butcher shop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבא, whom רב אדא בר אבא praised, takes responsibility. Pushing ahead of רבא's servant was seen as a slight to רבא himself. The list now has four חכמים, each with a different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: I am greater, or more important

phrases.english: And Rava said: I punished him,
because when he would go to the butcher shop
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets, through 'a piece of meat,' are part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: to take a piece of meat,
he said to the butchers:
I will take meat
before Rava's servant,
because I am greater than he is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth claim of responsibility, from רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא says the death came because רב אדא בר אבא pushed ahead of רבא's servant.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim and the daily review routine
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק also says he is the cause. The גמרא explains the background: he was ראש כלה, and every day he reviewed his lesson with רב אדא בר אבא before going in to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: I punished him. For רב נחמן בר יצחק was head of the כלה. Every day, before going in to the כלה, he reviewed his lesson with רב אדא בר אבא, and then he went in to the כלה.
steps.whatsHappening: A fifth חכם makes the same claim. Here the גמרא begins a longer story, starting with his daily routine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier claims, this one comes with a detailed story. The key background is that רב נחמן בר יצחק depended on רב אדא בר אבא every day to review the lesson. That sets up what goes wrong next.

keyTerms.meaning: Head of the כלה, the one who gave the public lecture
The large Torah study gatherings held in Elul and Adar
He would review quickly, or run through

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אֲנָא עֲנֵישְׁתֵּיהּ –
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: I punished him,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק רֵישׁ כַּלָּה הֲוָה.
phrases.english: for Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak was head of the kallah.
Every day, before he went in to the kallah,

phrases.aramaic: מַרְהֵיט בַּהֲדֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַבָּא לִשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: he would review his lesson with Rav Adda bar Abba,
and then he would go in to the kallah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אֲנָא עֲנֵישְׁתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fifth claim and begins a detailed story behind it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the death came because of him. The background is his daily review with רב אדא בר אבא.

steps.title: רב אדא is held up teaching others, and רב נחמן בר יצחק waits
steps.stepSummary: One day רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע stopped רב אדא בר אבא to learn רבא's teachings on מעשר בהמה. Meanwhile it got late, and he never came to רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: That day, רב פפא and רב הונא son of רב יהושע grabbed רב אדא בר אבא, because they had missed the end of the lecture. They said: Tell us how רבא said these teachings about מעשר בהמה. He told them: רבא said this, and רבא said that. Meanwhile it got late for רב נחמן בר יצחק, and רב אדא בר אבא did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. On one particular day, רב אדא בר אבא was delayed, and רב נחמן בר יצחק was left waiting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אבא was busy with something good: teaching other students what רבא had said. But it broke the daily routine, and רב נחמן בר יצחק could not do his review. This sets up the words he says in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They grabbed him, or held him
The tithe of animals, where every tenth animal is set aside

phrases.english: That day, they grabbed

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: (Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua)
Rav Adda bar Abba,
because they had not been there for the end of the lecture.
They said to him: Tell us
these teachings about the animal tithe,
how Rava said them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָכִי אָמַר רָבָא, וְהָכִי אָמַר רָבָא.
phrases.english: He said to them: Rava said this, and Rava said that.

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּהָכִי נְגַהּ לֵיהּ [לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק],
phrases.english: Meanwhile it got late for Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak,
phrases.notes: The name in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אָתֵי רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַבָּא;
phrases.english: and Rav Adda bar Abba did not come.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא יוֹמָא נַקְטוּהּ רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רב נחמן בר יצחק by describing the day the routine broke.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אדא בר אבא was delayed teaching רבא's laws, and רב נחמן בר יצחק was left waiting.

steps.title: "I am waiting for his bier" and the news of his death
steps.stepSummary: The students urge רב נחמן בר יצחק to begin. He answers that he is waiting for רב אדא בר אבא's bier, and just then word comes out that רב אדא בר אבא has died.
steps.simpleTranslation: The students said to רב נחמן בר יצחק: Get up, it is late for us. Why is the master sitting? He told them: I am sitting and waiting for the bier of רב אדא בר אבא. Just then, word went out that רב אדא בר אבא had died.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the high point of the story. רב נחמן בר יצחק says harsh words about רב אדא בר אבא, and right away the news of his death arrives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers sharply. Instead of saying he is waiting for רב אדא בר אבא, he says he is waiting for his bier. The news of the death comes immediately, so the timing ties his words to the death.

keyTerms.meaning: Master, a respectful way to address a חכם
A bier, the stretcher a dead body is carried on
Word went out, or a report spread

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: The Sages said to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak:
Get up, for it is late for us.
Why is the master sitting?
He said to them: I am sitting

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא מְנַטְּרָא לְעַרְסֵיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַבָּא.
phrases.english: and waiting for the bier of Rav Adda bar Abba.
Meanwhile, word went out

phrases.aramaic: דְּנָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַבָּא.
phrases.english: that Rav Adda bar Abba had died.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: קוּם, דִּנְגַהּ לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story. רב נחמן בר יצחק's harsh words are followed right away by the news of the death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן בר יצחק spoke of רב אדא בר אבא's bier, and at that moment the death was announced.

steps.title: Conclusion that רב נחמן בר יצחק was the cause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that it makes the most sense to say רב נחמן בר יצחק was the cause of the punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is reasonable to say that רב נחמן בר יצחק punished him.
steps.whatsHappening: Five חכמים claimed responsibility, and now the גמרא decides between them. It says רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim is the most convincing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The others pointed to earlier events. Only רב נחמן בר יצחק's words were followed right away by the news of the death. That direct timing is why the גמרא sides with him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable, or it makes sense
He punished him, meaning he was the cause of his punishment

steps.whatToRemember: Five חכמים each said רב אדא בר אבא's death came because of them. The גמרא concludes it was רב נחמן בר יצחק, because the death was announced the moment he said 'I am waiting for his bier.' The story teaches how serious it is to slight a תלמיד חכם, and how powerful a great person's words can be.
steps.whyThisMatters: It closes the story that began with רב דימי's figs. It shows how much weight חז״ל gave to the honor of תלמידי חכמים and to their spoken words.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק עַנְשֵׁיהּ.
phrases.english: And it is reasonable that Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak punished him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק עַנְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the timing in step 28 to decide among the five claims.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The most reasonable view is that רב אדא בר אבא's death came about through רב נחמן בר יצחק's words.

steps.title: The משנה: keep a new wall four אמות from a neighbor's wall and windows
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a person may not build a wall close to his neighbor's wall unless it is four אמות away. The same four-אמות distance applies to windows, whether the wall is above them, below them or facing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone whose wall was close to his neighbor's wall may not build another wall close to it unless he keeps it four אמות away. For windows, whether the wall is above, below or opposite them, the distance is four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a rule about how far a person must keep his wall from a neighbor's wall and windows. The required distance is four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives one fixed distance, four אמות, for two cases: a neighbor's wall and a neighbor's windows. Its opening words are worded in an unusual way, and the very next step of the גמרא questions them.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. The abbreviation מַתְנִי׳ marks where the משנה begins.
Four cubits, the distance required here

steps.confusionAlert: The opening words sound as if the first wall was already standing right next to the neighbor's wall. That is exactly the difficulty the גמרא raises next, so do not try to make full sense of it yet.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One whose wall was
close to the wall of his fellow
may not place another wall close to it

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִרְחִיק מִמֶּנּוּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: unless he distanced it from it four cubits.
The windows: whether from above them,
whether from below them, whether opposite them,
four cubits.
phrases.notes: He means that a wall built near a neighbor's windows must be four אמות away from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהָיָה כּוֹתְלוֹ סָמוּךְ לְכוֹתֶל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the story about רב אדא בר אבא ended with the conclusion in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wall must be kept four אמות from a neighbor's wall, and four אמות from a neighbor's windows, whether above, below or opposite them.

steps.title: How was the first wall allowed to be close?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the משנה's opening words. If walls must be four אמות apart, how was the first wall built close to the neighbor's wall at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first wall, how was it placed close?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. The משנה describes a first wall that was already close to the neighbor's wall, which seems to break the משנה's own rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires four אמות between walls, yet it opens by describing a wall that was already 'סָמוּךְ', close by. That seems to contradict the rule itself. The גמרא wants to know how this first wall could have been built legally.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה. The abbreviation גְּמָ׳ marks where it begins.
The first one, here meaning the first wall

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And the first one, how did he place it close?
phrases.notes: The 'first one' is the wall described at the start of the משנה, the one that was already close to the neighbor's wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the opening wording of the משנה in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's opening phrase 'מִי שֶׁהָיָה כּוֹתְלוֹ סָמוּךְ לְכוֹתֶל חֲבֵירוֹ'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires four אמות between walls, but its opening describes a first wall that was already close. That seems to describe something the משנה itself forbids.

steps.title: רב יהודה begins to explain the משנה's meaning
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the משנה should be read differently, and he introduces his reading with 'this is what it is saying'. His actual reading comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This is what it is saying:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the answer. רב יהודה announces that he will explain what the משנה really means, and his explanation comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'הָכִי קָאָמַר' signals that the משנה's words should not be read the way they first sound. רב יהודה will offer a clearer reading that removes the problem raised in step 31.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying. Used to introduce a clearer reading of a text.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: This is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה. רב יהודה's actual explanation comes right after this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer the question of step 31 by reinterpreting the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה (הָכִי קָאָמַר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to describe a first wall that was already improperly close.
steps.terutzMaskana: The full reading comes on the next amud. Here רב יהודה only signals that the משנה must be read differently.
